Antihero

/AN-tee-heer-oh/ - the stress falls on AN · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Antihero means a central character who lacks traditional heroic qualities.

The heist novel's narrator forges letters and lies to her partners, yet risks everything to free a stranger — a classic antihero whose chapters readers refuse to skip.

Worked Example

In the comic's first issue, the masked lead robs the armored car and keeps the money; by issue ten he is shielding the neighborhood with the same ruthlessness. The writers built him as an antihero: the story is his, but courage, honesty and mercy visit him only occasionally.

Antihero says something 'flawed main character' alone does not: the figure occupies the hero's place at the story's center while lacking the hero's virtues. A villain opposes the lead; an antihero is the lead.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

rogue: A rogue is a charming rule-breaker who can turn up anywhere in a story — sidekick, rival, comic relief. An antihero is specifically the story's central figure, carrying the plot while lacking the hero's usual virtues.

misfit: A misfit is someone who does not fit in with the people around them — the word says nothing about virtue or about leading anything. An antihero, by contrast, sits at the story's center, holding the audience's attention despite a thin supply of virtue.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

hero: a central figure with the courage and virtue an antihero lacks

idol: a figure admired as flawless — the opposite of a lead we follow despite the flaws

Where it sits · how much virtue the central figure carries — villain → antihero → hero

villain vs. antihero: A villain stops short of even an antihero's small ration of virtue: the villain works against the story's center, while the antihero occupies it.

hero vs. antihero: A hero goes further than an antihero on this ladder, bringing genuine courage and decency to the story's center instead of borrowed sympathy.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — anti

Prefix — anti: against; the opposite of (Greek)

Root — hero

Root — hero: the brave central figure (Greek heros)

Put it together

Put it together: Greek anti- means 'against' or 'the opposite of,' and a hero is the brave figure at a story's center. Bolt them together and you get the opposite of a hero standing exactly where the hero should stand — the same slot in the story, with the virtues missing.

Use the root in a new word: heroism

Use the root in a new word: heroism: The firefighters were honored for their heroism — the quality named for the same Greek heros that an antihero conspicuously lacks.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / literary

Antihero is the critic's precise label for a story's central figure who lacks the traditional virtues. Keep it off characters who are merely villains — they oppose the lead rather than being it — and off lovable rogues in the supporting cast. If the flawed one carries the story, antihero is the word.
